functions.name: add-user-to-function
functions.description: Grant one user access to a custom function already using named-entity distribution permissions.

appId.description: Containing app ID, required with callbackId.

userId.description: Slack user ID to grant function access.

callbackId.description: Function callback ID scoped to appId.

functionId.description: Encoded function ID instead of appId and callbackId.
Encoded function ID instead of appId and callbackId.

appId.description: Containing app ID, required with callbackId.

callbackId.description: Function callback ID scoped to appId.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_ad.description: One function selector and the Slack user to grant access.

permissionType.description: Resulting distribution policy reported by Slack.

users.description: Users with access reported by Slack, not a per-input success list; omitted if unreported.

items.description: A user reported by Slack as having access.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_a.description: The resulting function distribution permissions reported by Slack.

tags.instructions: Get the function selector from your function definition and a Slack user ID from your workspace directory. Use `list-function-permissions` to check the policy; it must already be named_entities. Use `update-function-permissions` to change the policy, or `batch-add-users-to-function` for several users. This does not create a user or a function.

functions.name: batch-add-users-to-function
functions.description: Grant up to 100 users access to one custom function already using named-entity distribution permissions.

appId.description: Containing app ID, required with callbackId.

items.description: Slack user ID to grant access.

userIds.description: Slack user IDs to grant access in one native request. Maximum 100 is a provisional local bound.

callbackId.description: Function callback ID scoped to appId.

functionId.description: Encoded function ID instead of appId/callbackId.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_ba.description: One function selector and 1–100 unique Slack user IDs to grant access.

users.description: Reported users with access, not per-requested-user success outcomes. Omitted when unreported.

items.description: A user Slack reports with access to the function.

permissionType.description: Policy Slack reported after accepting the native grant request.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_b.description: Slack-reported access state after accepting the grant, not individual mutation receipts.

tags.instructions: Use a function ID or app ID plus callback ID, and 1–100 unique user IDs. Check the policy with `list-function-permissions`; it must already be named_entities. Use `add-user-to-function` for one user and `update-function-permissions` for a policy replacement. The result is reported access state, not individual success receipts. After an ambiguous result inspect current permissions before retrying.

functions.name: batch-remove-users-from-function
functions.description: Revoke up to 100 users' explicit access grants from one custom function using named-entity distribution permissions.

appId.description: Containing app ID, required with callbackId.

items.description: Slack user ID whose explicit grant should be removed.

userIds.description: Slack user IDs whose explicit grants should be removed in one request; maximum 100 is a provisional local bound.

callbackId.description: Function callback ID scoped to appId.

functionId.description: Encoded function ID instead of appId/callbackId.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_ba.description: One function selector and 1 to 100 unique Slack users whose explicit grants should be revoked.

users.description: Reported users with access after removal; not input-correlated mutation outcomes. Omitted if unreported.

items.description: A user Slack reports as having access after removal.

permissionType.description: Distribution policy Slack reported after processing the native removal request.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_b.description: Slack-reported distribution policy and optional access state after the aggregate removal request.

tags.instructions: Use `list-function-permissions` to inspect access and obtain user IDs. Supply 1–100 unique users and one function selector. Use `remove-user-from-function` for one user. This removes explicit grants, not users, functions, workflows, or indirect team/organization access. The aggregate result is not a set of per-user success receipts; check current permissions after an ambiguous response.

functions.name: create-app
functions.description: Create a Slack app from a structured app manifest and obtain its credentials and authorization URL.

teamId.description: Workspace ID to select when the connection supports organization-level app creation. Omit to use the connection's workspace.

settings.description: App settings; external event-subscription registration is excluded.

manifest.description: Declarative Slack app manifest as structured JSON, not a serialized string. Keys retain the app-manifest specification's spelling. Notification subscription registration is not supported by this tool.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_cr.description: Create a Slack app from a structured manifest, optionally selecting a workspace.

id.description: ID of the newly created app.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID issued for the app.

signingSecret.description: Sensitive secret used to verify requests from Slack.

verificationToken.description: Legacy verification token returned by Slack; not a replacement for signature verification.

credentials.description: Sensitive credentials issued for this app; store securely.

authorizationUrl.description: Slack OAuth authorization URL; creating the app does not complete authorization or installation.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_c.description: The created app identity, sensitive credentials, and unchanged OAuth authorization URL.

tags.instructions: Use this to create a new app, not to install it. Use `validate-app-manifest` first when checking a draft, and `update-app` for an existing app. Store returned credentials securely. Repeating a call can create another app; do not retry an ambiguous result without checking your Slack app dashboard.

functions.name: delete-app-permanently
functions.description: Permanently delete an app created through app manifests.

appId.description: ID of the manifest-created app to permanently delete.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_de.description: The manifest-created app to permanently delete.

appId.description: ID of the app Slack acknowledged deleting.

deleted.description: True only after Slack acknowledges permanent deletion.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_d.description: Acknowledgment that Slack permanently deleted the target app.

tags.instructions: Use a known app ID from `create-app` or the Slack app dashboard. This deletes the app itself, not merely an installation, and cannot be undone. Manager connections can delete only apps created by that manager app. Use `get-app-manifest` first if you need a configuration backup.

functions.name: get-app-manifest
functions.description: Retrieve an existing app's configuration as a reusable structured manifest.

appId.description: ID of the app whose manifest is requested.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_ge.description: Identify the existing Slack app whose configuration should be retrieved.

appId.description: ID of the app whose configuration was retrieved.

manifest.description: Reusable Slack app configuration document. Domain keys, values, nulls, and empty collections are preserved; no transport envelope is included.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_g.description: The requested Slack app ID and its reusable structured manifest.

tags.instructions: Use a known app ID from `create-app` or the Slack app dashboard. Manager-app connections can read only apps created by that manager app. Use the returned manifest as the starting point for `update-app`; configuration replacement requires unchanged fields too.

functions.name: list-function-permissions
functions.description: Read a custom function's distribution access type and the users, workspaces, or organizations Slack reports as having access.

appId.description: App ID containing the function; required with callbackId instead of functionId.

callbackId.description: Callback ID from the function definition, scoped to appId.

functionId.description: Encoded function ID; use instead of appId and callbackId.
Encoded function ID; use instead of appId and callbackId.

appId.description: App ID containing the function; required with callbackId instead of functionId.

callbackId.description: Callback ID from the function definition, scoped to appId.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_li.description: Select one custom function by encoded ID or by its app ID and callback ID pair.

id.description: Opaque ID of this user, workspace, or organization.

email.description: User's reported email address; omitted when not returned.

username.description: User's Slack username when reported; absent for non-user entities.

items.description: One access entity reported by Slack.
Access entities present in this provider response, preserving provider ordering within each category. Missing categories must not be interpreted as empty.

permissionType.description: Slack's distribution access type; known values are everyone, app_collaborators, named_entities, and system. Unknown future values remain intact.

items.description: Kind of explicitly reported entity collection.

reportedEntityTypes.description: Categories for which Slack explicitly returned an entity collection, including empty collections.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_l.description: The function distribution policy and the access entities Slack explicitly reported.

tags.instructions: Identify the function by its encoded ID, or by its app ID plus callback ID from your function definition. Use `update-function-permissions` to replace access policy, and `add-user-to-function` or `remove-user-from-function` for individual named-user access changes. This returns one provider response, with no documented pagination controls. reportedEntityTypes distinguishes an unreported entity category from an explicitly empty one.

functions.name: remove-user-from-function
functions.description: Revoke one user's explicit access to a custom function using named-entity distribution permissions.

appId.description: Containing app ID, required with callbackId.

userId.description: Slack user ID whose explicit function grant is to be removed.

functionId.description: Encoded function ID instead of appId/callbackId.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_re.description: One user and exactly one function selector: functionId or appId with callbackId.

users.description: Users with access reported by Slack after removal, not a per-input result. Omitted when unreported.

items.description: A user with access reported by Slack after removal.

permissionType.description: Distribution policy reported by Slack after processing removal.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_r.description: The distribution policy and any users Slack reports after removing the explicit user grant.

tags.instructions: Use `list-function-permissions` to inspect the function policy and user IDs. Identify the function by ID or app ID plus callback ID. The policy must already be named_entities. This removes the user's explicit grant, not the user or function; other team or organization grants may still permit access. Use `batch-remove-users-from-function` for several users.

functions.name: update-app
functions.description: Replace an app's configuration with a complete manifest containing both changed and unchanged fields.

appId.description: ID of the existing app to reconfigure.

settings.description: Complete app settings; event-subscription registration is excluded.

manifest.description: Complete replacement Slack app manifest, including unchanged fields. Specification-defined keys are preserved. External event-subscription registration is excluded.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_up.description: The existing app and its complete replacement configuration.

id.description: ID of the app whose replacement configuration Slack accepted.

permissionsUpdated.description: Slack's permissions_updated indicator, when returned. This is not a guarantee of installation, authorization, or recipient access.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_u.description: The app whose configuration Slack accepted and its optional permissions indicator.

tags.instructions: Start with `get-app-manifest`, edit the complete document, and optionally check it with `validate-app-manifest`. This replaces configuration, not a partial patch: omitted settings are not promised to survive. Some configuration transitions cannot be undone. Manager-app connections can update only apps that manager created.

functions.name: update-function-permissions
functions.description: Replace a custom function's distribution access type and, for named-entity access, its user, workspace, and organization allowlists.

appId.description: Containing app ID, required together with callbackId.

teamIds.description: Complete workspace allowlist for named_entities; omitted means empty in this replacement. Not allowed for other policies.

items.description: Opaque Slack workspace ID.

userIds.description: Complete user allowlist for named_entities; omitted means empty in this replacement. Not allowed for other policies.

items.description: Opaque Slack user ID.

functionId.description: Encoded function ID, instead of appId and callbackId.

permissionType.description: Complete distribution policy selection, using Slack's documented values; system remains provider-defined.

organizationIds.description: Complete organization allowlist for named_entities; omitted means empty in this replacement. Not allowed for other policies.

items.description: Opaque Slack organization ID.

functionId.description: Encoded function ID, instead of appId and callbackId.

appId.description: Containing app ID, required together with callbackId.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_up.description: Function selector and complete replacement distribution policy.

users.description: Users with access reported by Slack, not per-input mutation outcomes; omitted when unreported.

email.description: Reported email address; omitted when unavailable.

username.description: Reported Slack username; omitted when unavailable.

items.description: A user reported by Slack as having access.

teamIds.description: Workspace IDs reported by Slack after the write; omitted rather than inferred from the request when unreported.

items.description: Opaque Slack workspace ID.

permissionType.description: Distribution policy reported by Slack after processing the update.

organizationIds.description: Organization IDs reported by Slack after the write; omitted when unreported.

items.description: Opaque Slack organization ID.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_u.description: Resulting distribution policy and entity data reported by Slack.

tags.instructions: Use `list-function-permissions` to inspect current access. Identify the function by ID or by app ID plus callback ID. This replaces access policy, not an additive grant. For a single named-user change use `add-user-to-function` or `remove-user-from-function`. Each team and organization list is limited to 50 IDs; the user list is limited to 100. Empty named-entity lists intentionally remove those grants.

functions.name: update-managed-app-permissions
functions.description: Request who may interact with a managed app before installation. Already-installed apps retain their current permissions.

appId.description: ID of the managed app owned by this manager connection.

permissions.description: Requested interaction audience: all members or only the app owner. An installed app retains its current audience.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_up.description: Managed app and requested pre-installation interaction audience.

appId.description: ID of the managed app whose request was processed.

permissions.description: Effective interaction permission returned by Slack, which may differ from the requested audience when the app is installed.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_u.description: Managed app and effective interaction permissions confirmed by Slack.

tags.instructions: Use an app ID from `create-app` or the Slack dashboard and its managing connection. This Enterprise Grid feature applies only before installation. An installed app is not changed; inspect the returned effective permissions instead of assuming the requested value took effect. This is not custom-function distribution access; use `update-function-permissions` for that.

functions.name: validate-app-manifest
functions.description: Check a structured app manifest and return actionable validation issues without creating or updating an app.

appId.description: Existing app ID to provide validation context; omit for a new-app draft.

manifest.description: Slack app manifest as structured JSON with specification-defined keys, not encoded text.

FunctionInput_slack_app_configuration_va.description: A structured Slack app manifest and optional existing-app validation context.

valid.description: Whether Slack accepted the manifest in this validation context; not a guarantee that a subsequent write will succeed.

message.description: Provider's explanation of the validation problem.

pointer.description: Provider's JSON pointer into the supplied manifest, when available.

items.description: One manifest validation problem reported by Slack.

issues.description: Validation issues reported by Slack; empty for a valid manifest.

FunctionOutput_slack_app_configuration_v.description: Completed manifest validation with actionable provider diagnostics.

tags.instructions: Use before `create-app` or `update-app`. Supply appId when validating for an existing app. A completed validation can return valid:false with messages and JSON pointers; that is a usable result, not a failed tool call. Successful validation does not install or apply the manifest.
